+Formulas are graded by their RECALCULATED value, not their formula text. Before grading, the
+file is recalculated with headless LibreOffice, then each cell's resulting value and type are
+compared:
+- A plain cell formula (=IF(...), =INDEX(...), =SUMIFS(...), =VLOOKUP(...), =SUMPRODUCT(...),
+  =WORKDAY(...)) recalculates correctly — keep it when the answer must track per-copy data.
+  But confirm the value it will RECALCULATE to, not merely that the text was written.
+- These do NOT reliably recalculate headlessly and grade as blank/stale: array/CSE formulas
+  (openpyxl ArrayFormula), dynamic-array functions (UNIQUE/FILTER/SORT), TEXTJOIN, AGGREGATE,
+  and any formula whose inputs are volatile (RAND/RANDBETWEEN/NOW/TODAY, directly or
+  transitively). For these, compute the answer in Python and write the LITERAL result (a real
+  number / str / bool / datetime) instead of the live formula.
+- A formula that evaluates to "" writes a BLANK cell and lowers coverage — if a cell must be
+  filled, make sure your result is a real value, not an empty string.
+Reuse the answer pattern the workbook already shows:
+- If cells inside or adjacent to the target range already hold the intended formula or label
+  pattern (or the same formula is visible on another copy of this workbook), reproduce that
+  SAME formula/criteria across the whole target range — do not invent a different variant, and
+  do not add extra conditions (an extra date bound, filter, or divisor) the existing formula
+  does not have.
+- EXCEPTION: when the instruction says the existing formula is broken/wrong and asks you to fix
+  it, correct it as instructed and compute the intended result from the raw source — do not
+  reproduce the broken version or its stale cached value.
Match the expected TYPE and format of each answer cell:
- If the target range already contains a worked-example cell, replicate its exact per-column
type and formatting — text stays text, a real date stays a date, a number stays a number —
and preserve any leading/trailing spaces the source keeps (do not strip them).
+- When your answer value is looked up or copied unchanged from another cell, give it that
+  source cell's own value AND python type — do not coerce a number into text or text into a
+  number/date, and never leave an unresolved "=..." formula string in an answer cell.
+- When you SPLIT or EXTRACT a piece out of a text cell, keep that piece as the original text
+  (str), preserving its spacing — do not parse the piece into a date or number, even if a
+  worked-example cell in the range happens to be formatted as a date.
+- When the instruction asks you to CONVERT or STANDARDIZE a whole value into a date/time/number
+  (e.g. "reformat as dd/mm/yy"), store a real datetime/number and set the cell's number_format
+  to the requested display pattern — the pattern describes how the cell should DISPLAY, not a
+  text string to write.
- If the instruction names the form a result may take (e.g. "the result may be #N/A" or the
"output result may be '-'"), write that exact literal for those cases, not a numeric
-  placeholder such as 0.
+  placeholder such as 0. Conversely, write a computed value in EVERY target cell the
+  instruction expects to hold a real result — do NOT invent #N/A, "-", 0, or a blank for those
+  cells; use such a placeholder only when the instruction explicitly says the result may take
+  that form.
- Rich-text and conditional-formatting cells are themselves the graded answer — preserve the
CellRichText / cell formatting, and never flatten them to a plain string.
2. Solution code that writes the modified file to output_path.
3. Verification code: re-open output_path and print, for each cell in answer_position, its
-   value and its python type. Confirm every cell the task requires is filled with the intended
-   value in a matching type (a rich-text or formatting answer keeps its special type, not a
-   plain string), and that no cell you meant to fill is unexpectedly None. If anything is
-   wrong, fix your code and write again.
+   value and its python type. Confirm ALL of the following; if any fails, fix your code and
+   write again:
+   a. Every cell the task requires is filled with the intended value, no cell you meant to fill
+      is unexpectedly None, and a rich-text or formatting answer keeps its special type (not a
+      plain string).
+   b. If any answer cell holds a formula that may not recalculate headlessly (array/CSE,
+      UNIQUE/FILTER/SORT, TEXTJOIN, AGGREGATE, or volatile inputs), recompute its result in
+      Python and write that literal instead — do not trust the printed formula text as proof.
+   c. If the range (or another copy) contains a worked-example or an existing intended
+      formula/value, run your logic on its inputs and confirm you reproduce it exactly; if not,
+      your interpretation is wrong — revise the logic, not just the output.
Reply without a code block when you are satisfied the saved file is correct.
If your code raises an error, the traceback will be returned to you; fix the code and try again.
